claim: formed San Francisco 1973 as Golden Gate Rhythm Section; Schon and Rolie ex-Santana; Valory and Tickner ex-Frumious Bandersnatch; Prairie Prince of the Tubes; Herbie Herbert; Dunbar hired Feb 1 1974, fired after Sept 2 1978 Day on the Green; Columbia after Feb 1974 showcase; Fleischman May to Sept 1977; Perry hired Oct 10 1977, debut Old Waldorf Oct 28 1977; Steve Smith ex-Montrose; Rolie left after Departure tour, Jonathan Cain replaced; Rock Hall 2017

single peaks: Wheel in the Sky 57, Anytime 83, Lights 68, Just the Same Way 58, Lovin' Touchin' Squeezin' 16, Too Late 70, Any Way You Want It 23; no Hot 100 entry for To Play Some Music, On a Saturday Night, Spaceman; album peaks Journey 138, Look into the Future 100, Next 85, Infinity 21, Evolution 20, Departure 8, Escape 1; Infinity/Evolution/Departure 3x Platinum, Escape Diamond; release dates Apr 1 1975, Jan 1976, Feb 9 1977, Feb 29 1980, Jul 20 1981

released Jan 30 1978, produced by Roy Thomas Baker, first album with Steve Perry, peak 21, 3x Platinum; writers Lights (Perry, Schon), Feeling That Way (Perry, Rolie, Dunbar), Anytime (Rolie, Schon, Valory, Roger Silver, Fleischman), Wheel in the Sky (Schon, Fleischman, Diane Valory); Perry and Rolie duet on Feeling That Way; Rolie lead on Anytime

released Mar 20 1979, Roy Thomas Baker, peak 20, 3x Platinum, first album with Steve Smith; writers Too Late (Perry, Schon), Lovin' Touchin' Squeezin' (Perry), Just the Same Way (Schon, Rolie, Valory); Rolie and Perry co-lead on Just the Same Way
began as Diane Valory poem Wheels in My Mind; lead single from Infinity, released March 1978; first Journey song on the Hot 100, peak 57; 2x Platinum

Perry and Schon; Perry wrote most of it in Los Angeles about LA, moved setting to San Francisco after joining; US release Aug 1978; peak 68; 2x Platinum; played at Giants World Series games 2010 (Perry led it at Game 2), 2012, 2014
written by Steve Perry; US release June 25 1979; B-side Daydream; peak 16 in November 1979; Canada 12; Journey's first Top 40 hit in the US
Evolution produced by Roy Thomas Baker, peak 20, over three million sold; Steve Smith recruited from Ronnie Montrose's band
Perry wrote it about a real breakup, per the Time3 liner notes: he saw his girlfriend kiss another man goodbye; extended fade of na na's
inducted 2017, performer category, Pat Monahan of Train inducted; inductees Dunbar, Smith, Valory, Perry, Rolie, Schon, Cain
